Design for the user's primary decision; make the relevant comparisons visible together.
Give quantitative claims appropriate units, periods, baselines, and denominators. A context selector passing does not prove the data is correct.
Prefer aligned tables, small multiples, and nearby explanations when they reduce comparison effort.
Use space for useful information; justify oversized headers, nested cards, and repeated decorative labels.
Calibrate density to the page's task and viewport. Preserve readable type, interaction affordances, and useful whitespace; do not maximize a density score.
Keep chart scales, missing values, and uncertainty honest. Review these visually and against chart configuration; DOM geometry cannot establish graphical integrity.
Treat these as Tufte-inspired design guidance, not quotations or universal layout requirements. Honor project design systems and explicit user feedback.
